learning: Iterations 0 to 6 show s-bend and slalom max_error on a 0.059 to 0.068 m plateau across span, footprint, lead and controller changes, while line losses stayed near 1. If wheel_track 0.10 with scaled gains lowers those excursions below 0.06 m, turn rate was the limit. If oval progress falls while steering oscillation rises, the gain scaling is too high and kp should drop further.
notes: Applies the agreed wheel_track 0.10 test to the iteration 6 design. Gains are scaled by 0.833 (kp 3.75, ki 0.21, kd 0.375) to offset the roughly 20 percent rise in steering gain from the narrower track. Geometry is otherwise unchanged.
rationale: Iteration 6 (50 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y 0.05, base 1.15, kp 4.5, ki 0.25, kd 0.45) is the best run so far at 355.3. Oval progress is 0.956 with 17 of 20 finishes, well above the 0.65 floor. The s-bend and slalom still end off-track with max_error 0.0682 and 0.0645 m, both above the 0.06 m line, and neither finishes. Line losses are about 1 per run and steering oscillation is about 0.2 to 0.25, so sensing is holding the tape and the excursions are turn-induced. The Builder's decision rule therefore applies: change wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 with no other geometry change. A narrower track raises the turn rate per wheel difference by about 1.2 times, so the effective steering gain rises by the same factor. To keep that gain near the proven level, I scale the controller gains by 0.10/0.12 = 0.833: kp 4.5 to 3.75, ki 0.25 to 0.21, kd 0.45 to 0.375. base_speed stays at 1.15, since the oval finishes with margin. The sensor array, footprint, body, wheel radius and mass are unchanged so the wheel_track effect is isolated. Expected result: s-bend and slalom max_error below 0.06 m, oval progress at or above 0.85, and steering oscillation not rising above about 0.3.
